Lehko is free and open source: %s

Weather comes from Open-Meteo, outage schedules from YASNO and DTEK (through the outage-data-ua project), exchange rates from Monobank and the NBU. No accounts, ads or tracking.

Before uninstalling Lehko, switch the home screen back to the TV’s own (or the TV may be left without one) and turn back on the apps you turned off with it.
Android TV lets only its debugging mode change the home screen. Lehko uses it on the TV itself, no computer needed.
Turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press “Android TV OS build” 7 times.
Turn on “USB debugging”: Settings → System → Developer options.
"3. Press “Turn on” and allow debugging in the window that appears (tick “Always allow”)."
Also turn off the stock launcher

Frees the most memory and removes its ads. It isn’t deleted and comes back when you switch back. Try without it first; if the Home button still opens the stock screen, turn it on. With it on, always switch back before uninstalling Lehko.
Bring back the TV’s home screen?
Lehko will turn back on every app it turned off and give the home screen back to the TV.
Connecting to the TV’s debugging service…
Allow debugging in the window on the screen: tick “Always allow from this computer” and press OK.
The TV’s debugging port is closed. Check that “USB debugging” is on. Some TVs also have “Network debugging” (turn it on), or need this from a computer after every restart of the TV: adb tcpip 5555
Debugging wasn’t allowed. Try again and press OK in the window on the TV.
This TV only offers “Wireless debugging” with pairing. Turn on “USB debugging” instead.

“%s” saved your Wi-Fi network, and turning it off would make Android forget that network. Go to Settings → Network & Internet, forget your network, connect again, then try once more. Or turn Lehko on without turning off the stock launcher.
Android didn’t accept Lehko as the home screen.
Done! Lehko is the home screen. Keep “USB debugging” on: Lehko uses it to check itself after TV updates.
Done! Lehko is the home screen, apps turned off: %d. Keep “USB debugging” on: Lehko uses it to check itself after TV updates.
Done! The TV’s own home screen is back, and every app Lehko turned off is on again.

Lehko’s home screen crashed several times, so the TV’s own home screen is back. Please report it on GitHub.
Lehko’s home screen crashed several times and couldn’t switch back by itself. Open Lehko settings and bring back the TV’s home screen.
After a TV update Lehko fixed: %s

Turned-off apps stay installed and use no memory. Press an app to turn it off or back on. Before uninstalling Lehko, turn them all back on: bring back the TV’s own home screen, or, if it is in use already, press “Turn apps back on” in Lehko settings.
This needs the TV’s debugging mode. First make Lehko the home screen (or just turn on “USB debugging”).

“USB debugging” is off, so Lehko can’t check itself after TV updates. Turn it back on in Developer options.
The TV forgot Lehko’s debugging permission. Open Lehko settings, press “Home screen”, then “Allow debugging again”.

Lehko couldn’t check which apps saved your Wi-Fi network, so it turned nothing off (turning off such an app would make Android forget the network). Try again in a minute, or turn Lehko on without turning off the stock launcher.
This is a system app of your TV. Turning it off is safe to undo here, but some TV features may stop working until you turn it back on.

Makes the remote’s star, YouTube and “all apps” buttons work while the stock launcher is off; the star can open the app chosen in Lehko settings. Every other button goes straight on, and nothing on the screen is read.
